clue.text: Monster in heap of straw getting at food

parts.note: a cock is a small conical heap of hay or straw, as in haycock
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A beast lurking in a haystack goes for the farmer's supper.
explanation.walkthrough: AT is taken as written; 'in' and 'getting' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatrice is a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg, whose glance could kill.

clue.text: Farm animal left to find cover

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A beast wanders off to shelter somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a hood or covering, as worn by a monk or fitted over a chimney.

clue.text: Copper is a good one who may wave his hands about?

definitions.meaning: copper carries electricity and heat well, so it is a good material of this kind

definitions.text: who may wave his hands about?
definitions.meaning: the person leading an orchestra beats time with his arms

explanation.surface: A police officer is praised as a fine fellow given to gesticulating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal that passes current is a good conductor, and an orchestra's leader is also called a conductor.

clue.text: It's excellent of the French to provide assistants

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-rate or excellent
des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun

explanation.surface: A French employer thinks it splendid to supply helpers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aides are helpers or assistants, especially to a politician or officer.

clue.text: Artist with tricky class — naughty boys?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of class are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter faces a difficult classroom full of badly behaved boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' looks like it describes the class of pupils, but it signals the rearrangement giving SCALS; 'with' joins the painter to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascals are mischievous scamps, usually boys up to no good.

clue.text: Awfully nice, she is from an Asian country

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of nice and she are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad is described as terribly pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese describes someone or something coming from China, a country in Asia.

clue.text: Fare always covers this zone

indicators.note: the words Fare always cover, or contain, the letters of the answer within them

explanation.surface: A transport notice says the ticket price always includes this district.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district, much the same as a zone.

clue.text: Aussie animals taking time to settle

parts.note: roos is short for kangaroos, Australian animals

explanation.surface: Kangaroos take a while to calm down for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To roost is to settle down for rest, as birds do on a perch.

clue.text: Not stupid when collecting silver — it is very popular

indicators.note: collecting means one phrase gathers the other into its middle

parts.note: all there means mentally alert, not stupid
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A shrewd person picks up silver, which is much sought after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' puts AG inside ALL THERE, between the R and the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all the rage is extremely fashionable, an idiom for widespread popularity.

clue.text: Had a drink and complained audibly

indicators.note: audibly means we hear the word rather than read it, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: whined means complained in a moaning way

explanation.surface: Someone drank and then grumbled loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To wine is to drink wine, often as in being wined and dined.

clue.text: Tumble down the ski slopes maybe for teatime treat?

definitions.text: Tumble down the ski slopes maybe
definitions.meaning: a fall on Alpine slopes, perhaps in Switzerland, is jokingly a Swiss tumble
a sponge cake rolled up round jam, served with afternoon tea

explanation.surface: A skier's fall is compared with a cake at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: A Swiss roll is a British sponge cake spread with jam and rolled into a log.
explanation.definitionFit: The cake's name read literally describes a roll, or tumble, on Swiss mountains.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink — team will need transport

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: After a drink, the team will need a lift home.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Sage put out becomes aloof

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of sage put are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wise man who is offended turns distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstage as an adjective means haughty or standoffish, a fair synonym for aloof.

clue.text: Partner from Amsterdam?

definitions.meaning: in Cockney slang 'my old ...' is a man's wife or partner
coming from the Netherlands, whose capital is Amsterdam

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a companion hails from Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means Netherlandish and, in London slang, a wife or partner.

clue.text: Acting group, one kept in as punishment and reprimanded

parts.note: the cast is the group of actors in a play
I is the Roman numeral for one
gated means confined to school or college as a penalty

explanation.surface: A troupe of players has one member detained and told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke or criticise severely, so castigated means scolded.

clue.text: Goddess making a mister naughty

indicators.note: naughty suggests the letters of a mister misbehave and change places

explanation.surface: A deity makes a man behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon.

clue.text: Football team with its colour becoming mucky

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United, an English football club
Manchester United play in red

explanation.surface: A football side's kit gets dirty on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United, known as Man U, play in red shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Manured ground has had dung spread on it, so it is literally covered in muck.

clue.text: He's abandoning hospital with leap, the one getting away

indicators.note: abandoning means the word left behind loses the other piece

parts.note: He's written without the apostrophe gives the letters HES
a caper is a playful leap

explanation.surface: A patient leaves hospital with a jump, making his getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes H out of HES to leave ES.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaper is anyone who breaks free, such as a prisoner who gets out.

clue.text: Religious woman that is seen joining saint in crowd

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit within the word for a crowd

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd of people

explanation.surface: A devout woman is spotted with a saint among a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a woman who performs sacred rites in a religion.

clue.text: Little boy will sit in nearly all these seats

indicators.note: will sit in means the boy is placed inside the shortened word
nearly all means the last letter of these is dropped

parts.note: Ron is a short form of Ronald, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A small child will perch on almost every one of these chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' leaves THES, and 'will sit in' puts the boy inside it; the surface's little boy on a big chair hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrones are grand ceremonial chairs for monarchs or bishops.

clue.text: Outstanding Christian organisation to depend on holy books

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a Christian charity
lie, as in 'it lies with you', means to rest or depend on
NT is the New Testament, a group of holy books

explanation.surface: A notable church charity relies on scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or striking, standing out from its surroundings.

clue.text: Country activity very much associated with ancient dynasty

parts.note: far, as in far better, means very much
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A rural pursuit is closely linked to an old Chinese ruling house.
explanation.definitionFit: Farming, growing crops and raising livestock, is the typical rural occupation.

clue.text: Fellow in charge supporting rising celebrity

parts.note: for means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word for a celebrity reads upwards

parts.note: a name, as in a big name, is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A man in charge backs a star on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NAME into EMAN, going up the grid in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreman is the worker who supervises a team or crew.

clue.text: What's not entirely exciting a person who yawns?

definitions.text: What's not entirely exciting a person who yawns?

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words exciting a person is used, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone asks what lacks the spark to keep a listener from yawning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: something not quite exciting leaves its hearer yawning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is someone who stares open-mouthed or yawns.

clue.text: Set down cheap drink

definitions.meaning: to put something down heavily or carelessly

explanation.surface: Someone puts down a bargain bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: To plonk is to drop something down heavily, and plonk is also slang for inferior wine.

clue.text: Trees in curved formations by lake

parts.note: arches are curved structures

explanation.surface: Trees grow in curving shapes beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Larches are deciduous conifers, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Buck perhaps wanting maiden — or many maidens!

parts.note: a buck is a male hare, so a hare is an example
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young man wants one girl, or perhaps a whole crowd of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's quarters of a household, or the group of wives living there.

clue.text: It certainly doesn't sound like her sort of song

definitions.text: It certainly doesn't sound like her sort of song

parts.words: It certainly doesn't sound like her sort of song
parts.note: a sacred song whose name is pronounced like the male pronoun 'him', so it sounds like his, not hers

explanation.surface: A song seems ill-suited to a woman's taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a religious song of praise, sung in church.

clue.text: Child finally restrained by troubled mother in Norwegian city

indicators.note: restrained by means the letter is held inside the other letters
troubled suggests the letters of mother and in are disturbed into another order
finally points to the closing letter of the word Child

explanation.surface: A child is held back by an upset mother in a Norwegian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a link to the definition but belongs to the fodder: 'troubled' makes TRONHEIM, and 'restrained by' holds D, from 'finally', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trondheim is a city in central Norway, its former capital.

clue.text: Wanting lots of food — no good being very thin!

indicators.note: no means the letter for good is absent from the word

parts.note: greedy means wanting a lot of food

explanation.surface: Someone hungry for plenty says it is no good being skinny.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means slender like a reed, so thin and spindly.

clue.text: Child falling over ending in the ditch

indicators.note: falling over means the word for a child is turned back to front

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: ending in points to the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A child tumbles and finishes up in a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: A dike, or dyke, is a ditch or channel, as well as an embankment.

clue.text: Craftsperson one mum and lad spotted at side of street

parts.note: ma is a word for mum
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A worker, a mother and her boy are seen by the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted at side of' puts ST at the front; ONE is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses stone, a craftsman.
